newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU member states asked about French EMU plan.
newsitem.headline: EU member states asked about French EMU plan.

text.p: EU member states have been asked their views on France's plan to use pension funds to help it qualify for monetary union following disagreement on the issue at committee level a European Commission source said on Monday.

A number of committees organised by EUROSTAT, the statistical arm of the European Union executive, have been discussing whether a transfer of 37.5 billion francs from France Telecom to French government finances was acceptable.
But the source said the committees had been unable to agree on France's plan, and a letter had been sent to EU member states asking for their opinion.
"There was no consensus, which is why we have taken a (decision) to get the written opinion of member states," the source said.
The source added that the member states had been asked to report back by Wednesday so that the information could be given to EU Economic Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy.
De Silguy would announce a decision probably next week.

At issue is whether the transfer of money to cover future pension liabilities at the state telecoms operator can be used by the French government in its accounting to reduce its public deficit next year to meet the Maastricht treaty criteria for European monetary union.
Separately, de Silguy's spokesman said the Commission had not taken a decision on whether France's plan would be acceptable for qualifying its budget for EMU.
"It is not true that the Commission has taken a decision," spokesman Patrick Child told Reuters.
Child was responding to questions about a report that an EU financial accounts committee had failed to recommend to the Commission that it accept the French plan.
The mark jumped half a centime in Europe on market talk about the report.
Child said the Commission had received details of what France plans and that it was examining them.

An advisory committee of statistical experts from EU member states had met, he said. "In the light of the result of that discussion and the technical considerations...they (EUROSTAT) will take a decision in the next few days or weeks."

In Paris, a French finance ministry official also said no decision had been taken either at the level of the European Commission or any EU working group on whether the transfer from France Telecom was acceptable.
